assets.content:
Subject: Would you put one MarketingOS draft under your name?
Preview text: Run a real offer, then check every fact, link and phrase before you decide.

Hi there,

MarketingOS starts with the material behind one real offer. It reads that material into compiled facts it is allowed to claim, then uses those facts to draft the launch or onboarding email you request.

You do not need to begin with a full sequence. Register your brand in your existing workspace, add the website material or pasted text for one offer, and request one email.

That gives you a bounded test: a concrete draft built from the offer material you supplied, so you can decide whether it is worth reviewing further for this campaign.

MarketingOS does not replace your approval. Check the draft’s facts, links, and brand voice before copying any of it into your sending tool.

Sign in and request one email → https://app.orqagent.com/login/

- the MarketingOS team

MarketingOS drafts campaign emails from supplied material, then exposes the evidence behind a completed campaign. Its Knowledge page shows the compiled facts, supporting quotations, evidence identifiers, strength labels, and gaps in the material.

Your existing account opens the workspace where both views are available. Inspect them before deciding which language is usable, which claims need checking, and what should be rewritten.

Sign in and inspect the campaign → https://app.orqagent.com/login/

- the MarketingOS team

brief.interpretation: This is a two-email onboarding sequence for invited early-access testers who already have a MarketingOS account, not a sales or public-signup campaign. The selected reader runs a small SaaS and has a real launch or onboarding offer to test; the sequence asks for one bounded product trial and then a careful review of its output.
brief.reader:
Selected audience (user-stated constraints): Invited early-access testers with an existing account who operate a small SaaS business and need launch or onboarding email copy..
No further recipient situation is established. Compiled market context is research to check for applicability, not a replacement biography.
brief.reader_segment: An invited pilot user with a live account who still has not pushed one real offer through it
brief.reader_profile_override: Invited early-access testers with an existing account who operate a small SaaS business and need launch or onboarding email copy.
brief.promise: A test on one real offer lets the reader judge a draft built from their supplied facts and inspect the evidence and simulated-reader diagnosis before deciding what is usable.
brief.orientation: MarketingOS turns source material for a SaaS offer into reviewed launch or onboarding email drafts that the account holder checks before copying into their own sending tool.
brief.arc: Email 1 moves from an unused account to the smallest meaningful test: supply one real offer and request one email. Email 2 moves from having a draft to judging it deliberately: inspect the compiled source facts and the simulated reader's specific points of confusion before deciding what to keep or rewrite.
brief.sequence_rationale: The sequence starts with action because these readers already have access and do not need a category lesson; explaining every review surface before a draft exists would increase the apparent commitment. The second email earns its place after the run by showing how to evaluate the result without treating an AI critique as customer-performance evidence. Both emails stand alone, use the existing-account login, and avoid unsupported claims about speed, savings, correctness, results, pricing, or continued access. The single thing the user could send us that would most change this campaign is one attributable pilot result showing the factual-error count and editing time for a real generated email.

emails.job: Get the invited tester to begin one bounded, real-product test by supplying offer material and requesting a single launch or onboarding email.
emails.single_idea: The smallest useful MarketingOS test is one email for a real offer, because the product first turns the supplied material into a set of facts the draft is allowed to use.
emails.felt_need: I need a launch or onboarding email for a real SaaS offer, and I need to be able to check what the draft says before using it.
emails.mechanism: The reader registers the brand, adds source material for one real offer, and requests one email. MarketingOS compiles the material into facts it is allowed to claim before drafting; the reader still checks the resulting facts, links, and voice.
emails.belief_shift: Before: trying the account sounds like committing to a whole campaign. After: one real offer and one requested email are enough to produce something concrete to evaluate.
must_not_say: Do not imply that a campaign or draft is already waiting in the account.
Do not promise that setup is quick, that generation is immediate, or that the first run will be complete.
Do not claim the compiled fact set guarantees an error-free or fully source-traced draft.
Do not assume what tools, templates, writers, results, staffing, revenue, list size, or deadlines the reader has.
Do not mention pricing, a free trial, public signup, testimonials, performance gains, sending, publishing, competitor research, audience research, LinkedIn, or the older orqAgent agent builder.
emails.objection: The draft could still say something about the offer that the reader would not approve under their own name.
emails.call_to_action: Sign in to your existing MarketingOS workspace, register the brand, add the real material for one offer, and request one launch or onboarding email.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether a draft grounded in the supplied offer material is worth reviewing further for this campaign.
emails.next_step_value: The workspace lets the reader register the brand, add real source material, and request the first email rather than committing to a full sequence.
emails.next_step_limit: The requested draft still requires the reader to check its facts, links, and brand voice before using it.
emails.subject_strategy: Make the bounded test unmistakable: one real offer and one email, without hype, urgency, a time promise, or an implied waiting draft.

emails.job: Get the tester to inspect the factual basis and simulated-reader feedback for the generated draft before deciding what to keep or rewrite.
emails.single_idea: The useful review is not a score taken on faith: the reader can inspect both the source facts behind the draft and the report showing what the simulated reader understood, where they stopped, and what they doubted.
emails.felt_need: I need to know which parts of this draft are grounded in my material and where an unfamiliar reader may lose the thread before I decide what belongs in the campaign.
emails.mechanism: On the Knowledge page, the reader can inspect compiled facts, supporting quotations, evidence identifiers, strength labels, and missing information. In the completed campaign's review report, they can inspect what the simulated reader understood, where they stopped, their biggest doubt, and suggested changes; these observations guide a human review rather than standing in for campaign results.
emails.belief_shift: Before: the output is another AI draft accompanied by an opaque AI opinion. After: the factual inputs and the simulated reader's specific diagnosis are visible enough to judge on their merits, while real recipient response remains unproven.
must_not_say: Do not call the cold reader a human reviewer or imply that it represents actual customers.
Do not present its assessment as measured opens, clicks, sales, conversions, or proof the email will perform.
Do not guarantee that every draft claim is correct merely because source facts are inspectable.
Do not add a second CTA asking for a reply, meeting, signup, purchase, or public registration.
Do not repeat the setup argument from email 1 or introduce pricing, testimonials, sending features, competitor research, LinkedIn, or the older orqAgent agent builder.
emails.objection: An AI assessment of an AI-written email does not prove how real recipients will respond.
emails.call_to_action: Sign in to your existing MarketingOS workspace, open the completed campaign, and inspect its Knowledge page and “Why it scored what it scored” report before deciding what you would keep or rewrite.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide which language is usable, which claims need checking, and which parts of the draft should be rewritten before it goes anywhere else.
emails.next_step_value: The account exposes the compiled facts and supporting material alongside a specific diagnosis of what the simulated reader understood, where they stopped, and their biggest doubt.
emails.next_step_limit: This review helps assess the draft itself; it does not establish how real recipients will open, click, buy, or otherwise respond.
emails.subject_strategy: Signal an inspectable review rather than a performance claim: invite the reader to look behind the draft at its facts and the point where the cold read broke down.
must_not_reuse: The smallest useful MarketingOS test is one email for a real offer, because the product first turns the supplied material into a set of facts the draft is allowed to use.

brief.voice_notes: Use direct, explanatory English with no greeting or personal signature. Refer to MarketingOS by name, use “reads,” “compiled facts,” “draft,” and “cold-read” where natural, and keep qualifications explicit. Avoid hype adjectives, generic AI language, and any suggestion that the older orqAgent agent-builder product is being offered.
